groups.name: Shows set in a U.S. city that is also the title's setting but never named in the title
groups.explanation: Albuquerque (Breaking Bad), Atlantic City (Boardwalk Empire), Baltimore (The Wire), and New Orleans (Treme) are all cities that are the unmistakable primary setting of a prestige TV drama whose title does not contain the city's name.

groups.name: TV characters who are the moral philosopher of their show — but are deeply personally broken
groups.explanation: Chidi Anagonye (The Good Place) lectures endlessly on ethics while being paralyzed by indecision; Rust Cohle (True Detective) delivers nihilistic philosophical monologues while being emotionally destroyed; Dr. Cox (Scrubs) espouses idealistic medicine while being a self-sabotaging cynic; Tara Maclay (Buffy the Vampire Slayer) is the gentle moral anchor of the Scoobies while suffering from profound self-worth issues rooted in her abusive past.

groups.name: Shows whose series finale was set at least partly in the distant past via flashback or time shift — not the show's present
groups.explanation: Yellowjackets, Pose, Halt and Catch Fire, and The Americans each concluded their series with a finale that used a significant time jump or period shift — either flashing back to an earlier era or jumping years forward — as a structural device to resolve their central emotional arcs, rather than ending in the show's established present-day timeline.

groups.name: Actors who played a parent who discovers their child has been living a secret life
groups.explanation: Carrie Coon (The Leftovers — her character uncovers her brother's hidden departure-cult involvement, and in later seasons grapples with her daughter's secret choices), Matthew McConaughey (True Detective — Rust investigates a cult whose victims include children kept secret from their parents), Zach Gilford (Friday Night Lights — Matt Saracen uncovers his absent father's hidden second life during wartime), and Melanie Lynskey (Yellowjackets — Shauna's daughter's entire secret social and romantic life is a running revelation to her mother) all played characters whose central dramatic turn involves discovering a child's concealed existence.
